title: Execution Scenario Orchestrator: Spec and Playbook
author: Marta Alvarez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document specifies the Execution Scenario Orchestrator (ESO), a cross-cutting component that composes, schedules, and replays representative end-to-end inference scenarios against the runtime. ESO is intended to:

- Provide a reproducible, versioned way to define complex multi-tenant workloads (prefixes, kv-cache warmup, mixed sequence lengths, burst patterns).
- Integrate with kernel scheduler hooks so scenario fidelity is preserved when testing scheduler changes.
- Produce traceable profiling artifacts consumable by the benchmarking suite and the profiling playbook.

Scope and audience: engineers owning runtime architecture, kernel-and-scheduling, profiling, and SREs running performance experiments or incident triage.

Design goals

1) Determinism and provenance: every scenario is a small, self-contained script with a hashable manifest and metadata (model version, quantization profile, hardware fingerprint).
2) Scheduler-aware playback: the orchestrator can attach scheduler context (priority, tenant-id, kernel-hint) to each request so the runtime executes the scenario as intended.
3) Observability-first: scenario runs automatically capture structured traces, kernel attributions, and per-token cost deltas and upload to the central perf store.
4) Lightweight chaos vectors: the orchestrator supports controlled perturbations (evictions, forced preemption, simulated NVLink degradation) to surface degradation modes.

Component overview

- Scenario DSL (YAML): declarative description of request series, injected events, and expected assertions.
- Runner: controller that materializes requests and submits them to a chosen endpoint (local sandbox, canary cluster, full production mirror).
- Scheduler Adapter: library that translates DSL affinity/priority fields into scheduler annotations and kernel hints.
- Collector: post-run artifact collector (traces, kernel telemetry, raw responses, golden diffs) with upload to perf-bucket.

Scenario DSL (conceptual example)

# A minimal scenario manifest in YAML. Fields must remain flat (no nested objects with unknown keys) for deterministic hashing.

manifest_version: "1.0"
name: "multi-tenant-burst-warmup"
model: "llama-13b-q4f16"
hardware_fingerprint: "g4dn-8nvlink-2026-03"
sequence_profile: "mix-small-medium-long"
timeline:
  - t: 0
    action: "warmup"
    params: "prefix_file=warmup-prompts.txt,concurrency=4"
  - t: 30
    action: "burst"
    params: "clients=120,shape=50%short-30%med-20%long,priority=production"
  - t: 90
    action: "evict"
    params: "tenant=tenant-42,reason=memory-pressure"
assertions:
  - type: "median-latency-below"
    value_ms: "200"
  - type: "tail-99-latency-below"
    value_ms: "800"

Scheduler integration

The Scheduler Adapter exposes three annotations consumed by the kernel mapper: kernel_hint (preferred kernel variant), priority_class (production/canary/batch), and affinity_token (NUMA/slot placement hint). When the runner submits requests it attaches these fields as HTTP headers (X-ESO-Kernel-Hint, X-ESO-Priority, X-ESO-Affinity) to preserve signal across transport layers.

Example headers (curl):

curl -X POST https://runtime-canary.internal/api/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
 -H 'X-ESO-Kernel-Hint: grouped-attn-v2' 
 -H 'X-ESO-Priority: production' 
 -H 'X-ESO-Affinity: numa-0:slot-3' 
 -d '{"prompt":"Summarize ..."}'

Profiling playbook integration

When an ESO run completes the Collector creates a run package and triggers the profiling playbook pipelines:

1) Minimal trace upload: we include per-request trace IDs and compact kernel-attribution CSVs.
2) Sampling policy: for runs > 10k requests, we apply stratified sampling by sequence length and priority class.
3) Correlation loop: perf store populates the run record with scheduler decision traces so the profiler can compute causal latency deltas associated with kernel selection.

Benchmarks and synthetic load harness

ESO can emit two modes of workload: synthetic (generated tokens for microbenchmarks) and recorded-replay (playback of production request surface with anonymization). The benchmarking suite consumes scenario manifests to run SLO-driven experiments.

SLO-driven experiment matrix (example)

| parameter | example values | notes |
|-----------|----------------|-------|
| concurrency | 1, 8, 64, 256 | cluster-dependent cap |
| sequence mix | 60/30/10 (s/m/l) | affects kernel crossing points |
| kv-cache state | cold, warm, hot | warmimplies prefix-caching |
| priority distribution | 90/10 prod/batch | scheduler stress test |

Runtime runbook: Replaying a production slowdown

Purpose: step-by-step guide to reproduce a reported production slowdown using ESO.

1) Triage and capture: collect the incident ID and the example request IDs from the status page.
2) Assemble a scenario: create a manifest that replays the failing requests (redacting PII), include the observed client headers and priority classes.
3) Select target: use a canary cluster that mirrors the production scheduler version and kernel set.
4) Run with tracing enabled: set environment variable ESO_TRACE_LEVEL=debug and run the runner with --collect-kernel-csv.
4a) If the slowdown reproduces, immediately tag the run with incident:<id> and notify SRE channel.
5) If the slowdown does not reproduce, run a higher-fidelity replay using recorded-replay mode with full affinity and session cookies (use only in secure sandbox).

Investigation checklist (what to look for)

- Kernel attribution spikes: sudden shift from grouped-attn-v2 to scalar-attn-fallback during medium sequences.
- Preemption events: scheduler logs containing "evict" + matching trace IDs.
- GPU metrics: duty-cycle drop, NVLink error counters, and sudden memory compaction events.
- KV-cache miss rate increase after eviction window.

Known issues and mitigations

- Issue: affinity headers not propagated by edge proxy in old canaries.
  Mitigation: upgrade proxy config to preserve X-ESO-* headers; work-around: include scheduler hints in body metadata.
- Issue: reproducibility variance when running on different NVLink topologies.
  Mitigation: include hardware_fingerprint in the manifest and pin to identical pool for replay.
- Issue: large recorded-replay runs can saturate perf-store ingest.
  Mitigation: use bucketed uploads and the incremental-collector option.

Release notes (summary of changes that introduced ESO)

- 2026-01-12: initial beta of ESO runner and DSL, supports warmup/burst/evict actions.
- 2026-06-03: Scheduler Adapter v1 added kernel_hint mapping and header propagation.
- 2026-09-22: Collector incremental upload and stratified-sampling policies added to reduce perf-store load.

Operational requirements and configs

Config keys (example table):

| key | type | default | description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| eso.runner.target | string | "canary" | target cluster: sandbox|canary|prod |
| eso.collector.sample_rate | float | "0.1" | fraction of requests to keep in full trace (0.0-1.0) |
| eso.scheduler.propagate_headers | bool | "true" | ensure X-ESO-* headers are forwarded by gateways |
| eso.archive.bucket | string | "gs://perf-bucket/eso-runs" | destination for run artifacts |

Security and privacy notes

- Recorded payloads must be redacted. The runner supports an anonymizer plugin that hashes or drops PII fields before uploading.
- Access controls: only members of runtime QA or SRE may run recorded-replay against production-mirrors. ESO enforces RBAC via OAuth groups.

Ownership and rollout plan

- Owner: runtime-infra team (primary), profiling team (secondary). Contacts: Marta Alvarez (runtime-infra), Kofi Mensah (profiling).
- Rollout stages: alpha (sandbox-only) -> beta (canary clusters, opt-in) -> GA (policy: default available to oncall).
- Acceptance criteria for GA: deterministic replay of previously recorded incidents in 90% of cases (same kernel selection and equivalent per-token latency within 15%).

Appendix: Example full scenario manifest and runner commands

# scenario.yaml
manifest_version: "1.0"
name: "incident-2026-299-replay"
model: "vicuna-7b-q2"
hardware_fingerprint: "a100-mig-4g-2026-05"
sequence_profile: "60%short-30%med-10%long"
timeline:
  - t: 0
    action: "replay-requests"
    params: "file=incident-2026-299-requests.ndjson,concurrency=32,priority=production"
  - t: 45
    action: "chaos"
    params: "type=evict,tenant=default,duration=5s"

# run in sandbox
eso-runner --manifest scenario.yaml --target canary --trace-level debug --collect-kernel-csv --upload-bucket gs://perf-bucket/eso-runs/incident-2026-299

Support matrix and troubleshooting quick tips

- If kernel CSVs are empty: confirm X-ESO-Kernel-Hint header propagation and ESO_TRACE_LEVEL.
- If reproductions differ by >20% latency: pin hardware_fingerprint and verify NVLink topology.
- If perf-store upload fails: retry with --incremental-collector and check bucket ACLs.
